cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 takes T3's 'assuming the silence means something' and labels both T2 and T3 as stories.
cells.limitation: T5 answers T4 but ignores the Realist's own T2 case for speaking.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 introduces observation versus story; T9 reuses it to critique the silent test.
cells.limitation: T10 adds only a tone note already implied by T6's framing.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Freely given friendship (T1, T3) versus maintenance effort (T2, T5) is examined.
cells.limitation: Whether the friend values the friendship less is never examined as the core worry.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 accepts T5's accusation risk and reshapes the ask into an invitation.
cells.limitation: T10's acceptance arrives quickly; Section D keeps disagreement but T10 smooths it.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates what was observed from the unknown why, with open disagreements.
cells.limitation: Section D says it narrowed to what to speak about; debate narrowed to how to test.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T6 restates T5's worry fairly before distinguishing accusing from inviting.
cells.limitation: T1 recasts saying something as a confrontation and performance review; T5 treats T4 as accusing.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8: if she is a low initiator, the silent test loses a friend and proves nothing.
cells.limitation: The Idealist never answers T8's cost directly; T10 shifts to the bothers-you condition.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T8 marks its time limit as going further than Dunbar; Stone paraphrases fit the book.
cells.limitation: T1's 'say nothing' sits uneasily with Emerson's essay prizing sincerity between friends (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: Section A separates the known pattern from the unknown reasons for it.
cells.limitation: T2 asserts the user's inner ledger and likely resentment as fact about the user.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T3 grants resentment risk; T9 concedes and narrows its T6 recommendation.
cells.limitation: T5 Realist abandons T2's case for one honest remark without acknowledging the shift.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names the unknown why and how much the imbalance matters to the user.
cells.limitation: The possible underlying worry, being less wanted than they want her, stays unnamed.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T4 and Section E build on lovely meetings plus contact lapsing when the user stops.
cells.limitation: Few user details exist; the debate uses them but adds little from their specific pattern.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E: doing nothing is choosing the friendship as it is if warmth is enough.
cells.limitation: Speakers' views on friendship effort dominate; the user's own priority is asked only once in D.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T8 names the stake of losing a good friend to an uninformative silence.
cells.limitation: T3 onward assume the friend is she; the user never gave a gender.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on bothers you, does not bother you, suspected low initiator, unsure.
cells.limitation: Whether she initiates with others or has life pressures never becomes a branch; D's now-or-later question feeds nothing.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks whether the imbalance bothers the user now or might later.
cells.limitation: User's alternative wants, reassurance of being valued versus sharing the load, never offered; T2 asserts resentment.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T3 surfaces the assumption that silence means something; T9 shows a test reads quiet as answer.
cells.limitation: The assumption that equal initiating signals equal caring is never named directly.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T1 versus T2: freely given friendship against fairness of effort.
cells.limitation: No turn asks which the user values more when warmth and reciprocity conflict.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T1 and T7 name fear of making the friendship feel like a review.
cells.limitation: Fear of rejection or of mattering less to the friend is never offered as a possibility.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E presents four conditions the user can test against their own feelings.
cells.limitation: Most branches hinge on how much it bothers the user, with few other handles offered.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E: light remark, do nothing, small specific ask, time-limited pause.
cells.limitation: The small-ask option appears only late (T9, Section E) and is barely debated.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T2 prices silence as resentment; T8 prices the test as possibly losing a friend.
cells.limitation: Costs of the small specific ask in Section E are never stated.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: if it bothers you and the friendship matters, a light remark becomes reasonable.
cells.limitation: No observable sign distinguishes low initiator from low interest; T7 and T8 give ungrounded few weeks.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T9 and Section E note silence alone will not reveal her reasons.
cells.limitation: Unknowns are listed in Section A but not ranked by which most changes the choice.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E: invite her to suggest the next plan, a small low-stakes step.
cells.limitation: T7 and T8's few-week pause has no basis in the user's facts.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T4 states the observation in plain words: you plan, she meets warmly, contact stops.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8 'That experiment' clearly points to T7's quiet test.
cells.limitation: T9 'Conceding the Idealist's point' could mean T3 or T7.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all inside the word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: T6, T9, T10 state changes of position explicitly.
cells.limitation: Realist's T5 contradicts its T2 stance; all three share one calm register and length.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely recap; Section E compresses the debate into branches.
cells.limitation: T10's tone point repeats T6's non-accusing framing.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T8: you may lose a good friend to a silence that proved nothing.
cells.limitation: Tension stays mild; the risk of learning she cares less is never voiced.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T10 Idealist moves from say nothing to silence as a slow leak, after T9.
cells.limitation: T5 Realist reverses T2's case for speaking with no earlier argument named as cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T3 Idealist: demanding proof of love in a currency she may not use.
cells.limitation: Realist and Clarifier speak in the same plain register as each other.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 friend into a ledger; T2 the ledger is already running in your head.
cells.limitation: Clarifier turns T4, T6, T9 carry no image or sharp line.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T7's quiet test introduces a fresh turn the later turns react to.
cells.limitation: Near-uniform turn lengths and steady tone across T1 to T10 flatten rhythm.

strengths: T4's observation-versus-story distinction is reused in T9 to show the silent test is also story-making.
Section E maps four options, including waiting, a small ask and a time-limited pause, each with a condition.
Concessions in T3, T6, T9 and T10 reshape positions while Section D keeps real disagreement open.
weaknesses: Decisive conditions in Section E rest on feelings; no observable sign separates low initiator from low interest.
The user's possible motives and fear of mattering less are never offered as alternatives; T2 asserts resentment as fact.
The Realist reverses from T2's case for speaking to T5's case against asking with no stated cause.

symptoms.observed: Low initiator possibility raised, but no observable sign to tell it from disinterest.
symptoms.evidence: If she is simply a low initiator, you may lose

symptoms.observed: User's inner state asserted as fact; alternative motives for wanting reciprocity never offered.
symptoms.evidence: But the ledger is already running, just in your head.

symptoms.observed: Realist drops its T2 case for speaking with no cause named.
symptoms.evidence: I will push back on asking at all.

symptoms.observed: Friend's gender assumed as she though the user never stated it.
symptoms.evidence: If I pressed her for equal effort

symptoms.observed: All three minds use similar turn lengths and one calm register.
symptoms.evidence: People differ a lot in how they maintain friends.

findings.description: Emerson's Friendship essay stresses sincerity and truth between friends; advising the user to say nothing may not fit that source.
Asserts the user is already keeping an inner ledger and that resentment is the likely outcome, with no basis in the user's message.
The friend is referred to as she throughout; the user never stated the friend's gender.

findings.location: T2, T5, T8 (Dunbar); T4, T6, T9 (Stone, Patton, Heen)
findings.description: Paraphrases are consistent with the general themes of these books but could not be checked against the texts.

rubric_fit_notes: The user's message is very short, which limits how much personal context C3 can draw on; ratings there reflect use of the little given.
The Emerson concern is from memory and remains suspected.
question_type_note: As a decision question about whether to raise the pattern, every cell was read as written, with Section E treated as the option map.
